title: CFTC Chairman calls Illinois crypto tax a 'sin tax'
summary: U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) Chairman Mike Selig has criticized the Illinois legislature, stating on X that it is "jeopardizing Chicago's future as a financial market hub" by imposing a so-called "sin tax" on blockchain technology.He argued that the relevant bill taxes cryptocurrency asset transfers even when no economic gain occurs. According to Selig, this reduces Illinois residents to needing government permission to hold property rather than being holders of property rights. He added that as blockchain technology transforms financial markets, the choice to tax wallets instead of fostering the crypto industry could symbolize the long-term decline of Chicago's financial market.The criticism follows Illinois Governor JB Pritzker signing the Digital Asset Privilege Tax Act, which imposes a 0.2% tax on crypto transactions and has sparked industry backlash.

title: Arthur Hayes again accused of using followers for exit liquidity
summary: BitMEX founder Arthur Hayes is facing fresh allegations of using his influence to treat his followers as exit liquidity. On-chain analyst Specter highlighted a recurring pattern where Hayes recommends a specific coin only to sell off his holdings shortly after. Specter cited HYPE, ZEC, and NEAR as primary examples, noting that Hayes sold all his positions just days after promoting the tokens. The analyst added that WLD and CARDS later followed the same pattern. This behavior allegedly repeated several times in June alone. Specter warned that Hayes is now actively promoting SYN, which could lead to another round of victims.
